name: Elaine McAllister
psychographics: Values routine and familiarity; dietary changes feel like a loss of independence. Prefers tangible, proven solutions over new apps or trends.
current_solutions: Uses a laminated card in her wallet listing her renal diet restrictions (low potassium, low phosphate); shops at the local independent greengrocer 'Donnelly's' because the staff know her by name and point out safe produce. Avoids supermarkets altogether most weeks.
frustration: Called the NHS helpline at 2:15pm last Tuesday after a ready-meal she bought from the Co-op was labelled "suitable for coeliacs" but the fine print listed wheat starch. She spent 45 minutes on hold before getting through to a nurse who calmed her down, but she now checks every label three times before opening a package.
decision_style: sticks to trusted local shops and brand names she has used for decades; never tries new products without a friend's recommendation
voice: formal and slightly weary; speaks slowly, often prefacing requests with "I do apologise but" and ending sentences with a questioning rise in pitch
